claim: ntfy ships as image binwiederhier/ntfy; the Docker image does not contain a server.yml so users must create and mount /etc/ntfy/server.yml plus a /var/cache/ntfy volume for the cache.db.
quote: the Docker image does not contain a `/etc/ntfy/server.yml` file ... docker run -v /var/cache/ntfy:/var/cache/ntfy -p 80:80 -it binwiederhier/ntfy serve --cache-file /var/cache/ntfy/cache.db

claim: Gotify runs from gotify/server (or ghcr.io/gotify/server); a single /app/data volume holds the SQLite database, images and certs and should be backed up, with default admin password set via GOTIFY_DEFAULTUSER_PASS.
quote: docker run -p 80:80 -v /var/gotify/data:/app/data gotify/server ... The /app/data directory stores the SQLite database, application images, and certificate files. This directory should be included in a backup.

claim: apprise-api runs as caronc/apprise:latest on port 8000 with /config, /attach and /plugin volumes and an APPRISE_STATEFUL_MODE env (hash/simple/disabled) controlling whether config is persisted; repo has ~1.2k stars.
quote: APPRISE_STATEFUL_MODE: simple ... volumes: ./config:/config ... Stars 1.2k ... Worker count calculated as (2 × CPU count) + 1 by default

claim: LinuxServer publishes lscr.io/linuxserver/apprise-api:latest, a rootless PUID/PGID image on port 8000 with /config persistence and APPRISE_ATTACH_SIZE control.
quote: image: lscr.io/linuxserver/apprise-api:latest ... environment: PUID=1000 PGID=1000 TZ=Etc/UTC APPRISE_ATTACH_SIZE=0 ... volumes: /config /attachments

claim: ntfy auth uses an auth-file SQLite db with auth-default-access (set deny-all for private), admin/user roles, granular per-topic ACLs and tk_-prefixed access tokens, managed via ntfy user add / ntfy access / ntfy token add CLI or declarative server.yml.
quote: auth-default-access: Fallback permission ... read-write (default), read-only, write-only, or deny-all ... ntfy user add [--role=admin] USERNAME ... Token format: Must start with tk_ and be 32 characters

claim: For TLS, ntfy either terminates directly via listen-https/cert-file/key-file or sits behind a proxy with behind-proxy:true and base-url; without behind-proxy all clients share one rate-limit bucket.
quote: behind-proxy: true ... Without this, all visitors are rate-limited as one ... listen-https: ":443" cert-file ... key-file ... Let the reverse proxy handle TLS termination

claim: Gotify auth is application-token based: an application is created in the WebUI/REST-API and its token is passed as a query param to push messages, with only the creating user able to see them.
quote: To authenticate as an application you need the application token ... curl "https://push.example.de/message?token=<apptoken>" -F "title=my title" ... Only the user who created the application is able to see its messages.

claim: A homelab comparison rates Gotify's install as easy with ~5 env vars while ntfy needs more setup plus CLI user/ACL management, but finds ntfy more complete with finer permissions.
quote: The installation was not hard but required a bit of more setup for Ntfy, and Easy installation process for Gotify ... Ntfy additionally requires CLI commands to manage users and permissions

claim: Gotify uses under 50 MB of RAM and runs on the smallest VPS or Raspberry Pi, with a typical Docker memory limit of 128M.
quote: Gotify is extremely lightweight, using less than 50 MB of RAM, so it runs happily on even the smallest VPS or Raspberry Pi ... memory: 128M
